beats.text: Your friends have more friends than you. Watch why.
Here's a friend group. One person knows almost everyone.
Now everyone compares their friend count with their friends' average.
Most have fewer friends than their friends! In a real high school, it was fifty-five percent of the girls.
The popular one shows up in everyone's list. It's math, not you. That's why

sources: Feld (1991), Why your friends have more friends than you do, American Journal of Sociology 96(6), 1464–1477 – the 'friendship paradox': popular people appear in many friend lists, so the mean number of friends of friends exceeds the mean number of friends; in Coleman's Marketville high-school data 80 of 146 girls (55%) had fewer friends than the mean of their friends, 41 had more, 25 the same.
Simulation: a made-up group of 26 people with one very popular person; 23 of 26 have fewer friends than the average of their friends.
